[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Count of Range Sum** [LC 327 · Count of Range Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-of-range-sum/){difficulty="Hard"}

A subarray sum is a difference of prefix sums: $\mathit{sum}(i..j) = P[j{+}1] - P[i]$, where $P[0] = 0$ and $P[k] = \mathit{nums}[0] + \cdots + \mathit{nums}[k{-}1]$. So the problem is: **count pairs $i < j$ with $\mathit{lower} \le P[j] - P[i] \le \mathit{upper}$**, i.e. $P[i] \in [P[j] - \mathit{upper},\; P[j] - \mathit{lower}]$. Scan $j$ from left to right and keep every earlier $P[i]$ in a multiset that answers "how many stored values lie in $[a, b]$?" — the @sec-coord-a2 Fenwick tree, over **compressed prefix sums**: collect all $n + 1$ prefix sums up front (the whole input is known: offline), sort the distinct ones, and index the tree by rank. A value query becomes two rank queries plus a subtraction, and each prefix sum is a single point add. The compression is legal because the question "is $P[i]$ between $a$ and $b$?" is pure order — @sec-coord-a1's certificate.

[Solved in full in @sec-coord-p1-rangesum.]{.card-link}

:::
